purpose: Teach: ハブ/シューズ/マックス/サバ/鷹/樹脂/メダル/必修

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃の駅、今は、立派なハブ駅になっているな、覚えてる、ばあさん?
lines.en: The station from when I was young — it's become quite the grand hub now. You remember, don't you?
lines.style: Soft, nostalgic opening. Voice settles into a gentle reminiscence. Pace unhurried, as if turning something over in memory. Slight rise at the end — inviting her in, not challenging.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。あなたの革のシューズ、お祖父ちゃんが、長年、使っていたわよね、覚えてる?
lines.en: Mm-hmm. Those leather shoes of yours — Grandfather wore them for so many years. You remember that, don't you?
lines.style: Quiet, tender agreement. Speaks slowly, as if touching the memory itself. Warm without nostalgia — more present affection. Trailing question mark is genuine, not rhetorical.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃の私、声、マックスで、応援していたな、息子の試合、本当に。
lines.en: When I was young, I'd cheer at your brother's matches with my whole voice. I really did.
lines.style: Voice softens but carries conviction. Slight breathiness, as if moved by his own memory. Emphasises the commitment — the fullness of it. Fades gently on the final phrase.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 昔の食卓、サバ料理、よく出していたわよね、お父さんが、好きだったから。
lines.en: At the old dinner table, I'd make mackerel dishes often — your father loved them so.
lines.style: Warm, settled tone. Speaks as if standing in that kitchen again. No rush. Slight tenderness on the mention of her husband's preference — a small, specific love remembered.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、鷹狩りの本、よく、読んでいたな、私、覚えてるよ。
lines.en: Your grandfather — when he was young, he read books about falconry all the time. I still remember that.
lines.style: Quieter, more reflective. Voice carries the weight of watching someone you love. Measured pace. The final phrase has certainty — this memory has settled into him like fact.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 昔の樹脂の食器、軽くて、使いやすかったわよね、子育ての時、便利だったわ。
lines.en: Those old plastic dishes were so light and practical — they made raising children so much easier.
lines.style: Practical warmth underneath the nostalgia. Speaks with a kind of grateful remembrance of small things. Not wistful exactly — more grounded in the useful love of survival and care.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 息子が、若い頃、メダル、たくさん、取ってきたな、本当に、嬉しかった、私たち。
lines.en: When your son was young, he brought home so many medals. We were truly proud.
lines.style: Voice lifts with genuine warmth and pride. Opens bright. Pace steady and sure. The 'we' carries weight — shared joy between two people who watched it happen together.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お父さんの代、大学の必修科目、結構、厳しかったって、よく、話してくれたわよね。
lines.en: Your father used to tell me how strict his university requirements were. He'd mention it quite often.
lines.style: Reflective, conversational. Speaks as if listening to those old conversations again. Warm undercurrent — noticing he needed to talk about it. Fades at the end, satisfied with the memory.
